correctness.rationale: The classical matching-complex connectivity theorem makes M(K8) simply connected; the opposite-edge perfect matching gives a global fixed barycenter and Armstrong gives pi1=0 for the quotient. The standalone exact integral verifier reconstructs 763 matching faces and all barycentric flag-orbits, verifies signed d^2=0, computes quotient cell counts (107,576,804,318), and performs 106+470+318 unimodular unit-pivot chain contractions to residual ranks (1,0,16,0), with no nonzero remaining differential. These are exact integer operations, not merely modular samples. Hurewicz and the homology Whitehead theorem give the wedge of sixteen two-spheres.

value.rationale: The first simply connected complete-graph matching complex has a natural nonfree full cyclic action. Determining its complete integral orbit-space homotopy type resolves torsion and higher attachment ambiguity beyond known upstairs sphere-wedge and rational invariant information. The sixteen-sphere quotient is a natural exact symmetry invariant, and the contrast to 132 spheres upstairs is topologically informative.
